title: cost-optimization-autotune-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for hosted and dedicated customers by automatically selecting batching/caching defaults and quantization profiles per workload. This PR implements an initial autotune service, default policy updates, quantization profile catalog, and unit-economics (uecon) tooling for visibility and simulation.

What this PR does: adds an autotune controller that observes latency and throughput signals and recommends (and optionally applies) batching window, max batch size, and prefix/KV cache TTL defaults. Adds a small catalog of quantization profiles for common GPU classes (T4, A10, A100) with heuristics to pick safe defaults based on sequence length and accuracy budget. Introduces a uecon CLI and a minimal dashboard to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs and project monthly spend given traffic patterns.

Design notes: the autotune controller runs as a leader-election service and writes recommendations to engine/config/autotune_recommendations.yaml. Changes are gated behind the feature flag feature.autotune_apply; defaults are read from engine/config/batching_defaults.yaml and can be overridden per-customer. Quant profiles are additive and non-breaking: model-serving continues to support explicit per-model config. The uecon tooling uses historical trace samples to compute expected tokens-per-request and applies quant/ batching/caching profiles to compute projected spend.

Checklist: [x] implement controller core loop and candidate scoring [x] add batching/caching defaults and config schema [x] quant profile catalog and selection heuristics [x] uecon CLI + minimal console widget [x] unit and integration tests [x] docs and migration notes

Testing: unit tests for scheduler heuristics (tests/autotune/test_scheduler.py), integration test that runs a synthetic traffic profile against the local runtime and asserts latency SLO and cost delta. CI initially flagged a flaky e2e that was due to a timing assumption; fixed by adding a jitter-aware assertion. Performance testing on staging shows median token cost reduction ~18% for conversational workloads with typical seq_len 256 and ~12% for long-document workloads, with <2% regression in output quality for quantized profiles flagged as "recommended".

Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature.autotune_apply. Start with recommendations-only mode for 2 weeks, monitor uecon dashboard and quality regression alerts. Gradually enable auto-apply for low-risk tiers (internal customers, dedicated non-prod) before enabling for hosted customers.

Related: Linear ENG-8421, PM-1293; Support ticket SUP-412 for customer request to reduce inference spend.

Notes for reviewers: focus on controller failure modes and config schema compatibility. The majority of changes are additive; the only mutable surface is the default YAML and the new leader service. If merged, follow-up PR will add per-customer rollout controls and canary policies to Redwood Console

release_notes: Add autotune controller to recommend batching/caching defaults, introduce quantization profile catalog for safe defaults across GPU classes, and ship initial unit-economics (uecon) tooling (CLI + dashboard). Rollout is behind feature.autotune_apply; non-breaking and opt-in by default.
expected_impact: Estimated median token cost reduction ~15-20% for conversational workloads; low-risk rollout with recommendation-only phase. Monitor quality regression alerts and uecon dashboard.
migration_notes: No forced migrations. Defaults are additive; customers with explicit per-model configs are unaffected. Ops: add feature.autotune_apply=false to opt-out during rollout if needed. Ensure k8s autoscaler has cpu/memory buffers for leader pod.
